The story behind the collection

A little help from BÄSINGEN

When Sarah Fager began conceptualising the BÄSINGEN collection, she did so with a clear goal: to create beautiful, inclusive designs for the many that support the independence of people of all ages in the most important place – our own homes. Let’s see how she brought her ambitious collection into the world.

If you were to visit an IKEA and see the BÄSINGEN collection on the store floor, you’d think it was an attractive, minimalist addition to our standard range. And you’d be right. But the BÄSINGEN collection comes with something extra special. Each of the six products has hidden features that hope to give people who have or encounter challenges at home a helping hand.

When designer Sarah Fager started working on the collection, she was immediately entranced by design thinking challenges she hadn’t faced before. "At IKEA, we do our product development in an open environment,” says Sarah. “Because people are always walking around, we get feedback constantly. When we show our prototypes there, people sit down and ask questions and sometimes, we ask people to take objects home and test them.”

“We wanted to create something that fits with our range, coordinated with the Scandinavian, minimalistic style that we have at IKEA. We tried different colours but landed on anthracite as it works well as a contrast when placed in spaces which are often lighter, like the bathroom,” says Sarah.

The step stools

Practicality and beauty in one! The step stools add both to the kitchen and bathroom. The lacquered metal is a stylish contrast to the textured plastic, and the curved handrail on each product offers added support and aesthetic interest.

The shower solutions

Inspired by the insight that many people experience impactful changes that can make something as simple as taking a shower challenging. By adding a chair, or a shower shelf with a hidden integrated handle, you can give people added support and improve their independence – making shower time more relaxing and enjoyable.

The grip bars

For people looking for a towel rail, or a toilet roll holder, that is exactly what they will see when they look at the BÄSINGEN collection. For people looking for extra support, they will note the grips added to the design. That was precisely what Sarah aimed for with this collection: to be beautiful to everyone, with hidden functionality for those who need it.

"BÄSINGEN mirrors our commitment to Democratic Design – where form, function, quality, sustainability, and low price come together to create a better life for the many people."

– Sarah Fager

https://www.ikea.com/global/en/stories/d.visible_text: Behind the BÄSINGEN collection – IKEA Global Skip to main content Stories Jobs Newsroom Our business Open main menu Close main menu Stories Jobs Newsroom Our business The story behind the collection A little help from BÄSINGEN When Sarah Fager began conceptualising the BÄSINGEN collection, she did so with a clear goal: to create beautiful, inclusive designs for the many that support the independence of people of all ages in the most important place – our own homes. Let’s see how she brought her ambitious collection into the world. Play video of Sarah with a BÄSINGEN shower chair. If you were to visit an IKEA and see the BÄSINGEN collection on the store floor, you’d think it was an attractive, minimalist addition to our standard range. And you’d be right. But the BÄSINGEN collection comes with something extra special. Each of the six products has hidden features that hope to give people who have or encounter challenges at home a helping hand. When designer Sarah Fager started working on the collection, she was immediately entranced by design thinking challenges she hadn’t faced before. "At IKEA, we do our product development in an open environment,” says Sarah. “Because people are always walking around, we get feedback constantly. When we show our prototypes there, people sit down and ask questions and sometimes, we ask people to take objects home and test them.” “We wanted to create something that fits with our range, coordinated with the Scandinavian, minimalistic style that we have at IKEA. We tried different colours but landed on anthracite as it works well as a contrast when placed in spaces which are often lighter, like the bathroom,” says Sarah. The step stools Practicality and beauty in one! The step stools add both to the kitchen and bathroom. The lacquered metal is a stylish contrast to the textured plastic, and the curved handrail on each product offers added support and aesthetic interest. The shower solutions Inspired by the insight that many people experience impactful changes that can make something as simple as taking a shower challenging. By adding a chair, or a shower shelf with a hidden integrated handle, you can give people added support and improve their independence – making shower time more relaxing and enjoyable. The grip bars For people looking for a towel rail, or a toilet roll holder, that is exactly what they will see when they look at the BÄSINGEN collection. For people looking for extra support, they will note the grips added to the design. That was precisely what Sarah aimed for with this collection: to be beautiful to everyone, with hidden functionality for those who need it. 1/2 1 of 2 Play video 1/2 1 of 2 "BÄSINGEN mirrors our commitment to Democratic Design – where form, function, quality, sustainability, and low price come together to create a better life for the many people." – Sarah Fager KUNGSCISSUS Year: 2023 Design: Emma Hagman ANNIKEN Year: 2014 Designer: Ida Pettersson Preutz FREDRIKA Year: 2007 Design: Helen Trast TÅSTRUP Year: 2012 Design: HC Ericson International Sales • Inter IKEA Group • IKEA Foundation • IKEA Museum • IKEA Social Entrepreneurship • FAQs Cookie settings • Privacy & Cookie statement • Contact IKEA / Submit complaint • Sitemap • Legal © Inter IKEA Systems B.V. 1999 - 2026

Have a question? We are happy to help.

The IKEA business spans a wide range of areas, organisations and companies. To help you find the right contact, we've put together commonly asked questions, including contact details.

There are no IKEA stores in the country where I live. How can I buy IKEA products?

IKEA stores are only allowed to sell within the country where they are located. To learn about placing an order from outside our active markets, visit our International Sales page.

How do I become an IKEA supplier?

We are always looking for new suppliers who share our passion for quality and sustainability.

Visit our supplier page where you will find the application form.

I’m interested in becoming an IKEA franchisee. Where can I find out more?

Inter IKEA Systems B.V., the IKEA franchisor, is constantly evaluating potential IKEA franchisees in both new and existing markets. When considering new franchisees, Inter IKEA Systems B.V. evaluates attributes such as:

- experience local market knowledge and presence (demonstrating ability to set up and operate IKEA stores nationally) - corporate culture and values

- financial strength and ability to complete the investment process across a country and in a large-scale retail environment format.

Send an email to [email protected] telling us why you would like to become a franchisee.

Where can I find IKEA reports and publications?

To make finding reports and publications easier, we have gathered them in one place.

Browse and download recent IKEA publications and reports.

How can I apply for permission to use IKEA copyright images/films?

We tend to grant permission for educational and training purposes and deserving causes. Material that does not fit under either of these categories is assessed on a case by case basis since we want to know the context in which the material will be used.

For more information, send a mail to [email protected].

How can I report misuse of the IKEA trademark that I have come across?

The IKEA trademark is sometimes used without our permission. It is very important to us that our consumers are not misled, and that they can have confidence that all products bearing the IKEA trademark are genuine products.

We therefore ask you to help us by reporting any wrongful use of the IKEA trademark or similar marks by sending a mail to [email protected]. We cannot give you any reward or compensation, but you will get a big thank you for your support in protecting the IKEA trademark and preventing fraud and misrepresentation.

I observed or experienced a breach of code of conduct, e.g. involving corruption, harassment, discrimination. How do I raise my concern?

It is often possible to address a concern directly with the person involved. However, sometimes a more neutral way of reporting is better or feels more suitable. There are different channels to report depending on where in the IKEA value chain the potential breach has occurred:

IKEA Retail: If you want to raise a concern related to the IKEA stores or other parts of the retail business, please refer to the IKEA retailer in the market in question here.

IKEA Suppliers: If you want to raise a concern related to direct or indirect suppliers to IKEA, go here.

Inter IKEA Group: To raise concerns related to Inter IKEA Group co-workers, go here.

IKEA Foundation: If you want to raise a concern related to the IKEA Foundation, or the work it supports, visit ikeafoundation.org.

Didn't find what you were looking for? Try these other websites:

Inter IKEA Group

Inter IKEA Group is the group of companies that connects IKEA franchisees with range development and suppliers, and aligns the overall IKEA strategic direction.

IKEA Foundation

IKEA Foundation is the philanthropic arm of INGKA Foundation. IKEA Foundation focuses on improving the lives of vulnerable children by enabling their families to create sustainable livelihoods, and to fight and cope with climate change.

IKEA Museum

Situated in the building that housed the very first IKEA store, the IKEA Museum is for anyone who iscurious about the IKEA brand and invites visitors to follow our development decade by decade.

IKEA Social Entrepreneurship B.V.

IKEA Social Entrepreneurship is all about creating opportunities for vulnerable and marginalised people. By backing and working with social entrepreneurs, we contribute to better everyday lives around the world.

ITCS Lab

ITCS is a test lab and training centre for our suppliers and co-workers. ITCS lab is owned by IKEA.

Inter IKEA Foundation

Based in Liechtenstein, Inter IKEA Foundation is the ultimate owner of Inter IKEA Group.

IKEA PS 2026

Since 1995, the IKEA PS collection has stood for good design and function at a low price. New for 2026 is a collection of more than 40 products celebrating playful functionality.

Up for some fun?

10 quiz questions to tickle your PS curiosity, with insider scoops on how the new products came to be.

IKEA PS 2026 Chair-bed

Design Matilda Lindstam Nilsson

Function, comfort and fun in one! With its low, pocket-sprung seat and cushions cradled in tubular steel, this chair-bed gives a playful nod to the '70s.

IKEA PS 2026 Cabinet

Design Friso Wiersma

A celebration of the craftsmanship of IKEA's skilled woodworkers, the character of this woven pine masterpiece only grows more attractive over time.

IKEA PS 2026 LED portable lamp

Design Alexander Pott

"Part cylinder, part Christmas bauble and part petri dish," is how Lex Pott describes the shape of this portable lamp, available in three colour options.

IKEA PS 2026 Vase

Design Maria Vinka

Hand blown by skilled craftspeople, the delightfully surprising ears give each vase its unique expression and one-of-a-kind character.

IKEA PS 2026 Stool

Design Mikael Axelsson

See the teeth on this solid birch stool? They're not just a clever design detail, but an unapologetically low-tech height-adjustment mechanism.

IKEA PS 2026 3-seat sofa-bed

Design Ola Wihlborg

Built with the same foam and supportive pocket spring design as a mattress, Ola’s sofa bed feels as good as it looks.

IKEA PS 2026 Easy chair

Design Ellen Hallström

This playfully elegant easy chair highlights the best qualities of plywood – with a simple construction that pieces together like a jigsaw puzzle.

IKEA PS 2026 Table clock

Design Marta Krupińska

No, that's not a submarine surfacing in your living room! This playful table clock features a periscope-inspired form in bright red; sure to add cheer and make a splash in any space.

IKEA PS 2026 Bench

Design Marta Krupińska

This fun bench is so much more than a seat: it encourages you to sit – alone or with a loved one – for a moment of pure, unadulterated silliness!

IKEA PS 2026 Easy chair

Design Mikael Axelsson

Inspired by our INNERLIG inflatable sofa from the 1990s – which, frankly, fell flat – this easy chair update is as comfortable as a regular chair, with minimised material usage and shipping volume.

IKEA PS 2026 Rug, low pile

Design Michelle Armas

Created using a special blooming ink technique, each shape on this rug represents souls. “The flowing ink is those souls communicating," explains Michelle.

IKEA PS 2026 Cushion cover

Design Michelle Armas

This dreamy cushion cover features flowing ink shapes in vibrant shades of blue, green and orange. The Atlanta-based artist owes her love of colour to her creative upbringing in a vibrant Spanish family.

IKEA PS 2026 Table

Design Ola Wihlborg

Even a small home needs a big table sometimes! Just a quick twist of its signature red-wing screw and this folding table collapses away.

IKEA PS 2026 Glass-door cabinet

Design Ola Wihlborg

A stylish way to keep your treasures dust-free. As for the mesh – surprise! – there actually isn't any. The glass has a printed grid pattern that mimics the look of metal, minus the trouble of keeping it clean.

IKEA PS 2026 Vase

Design Maria Vinka

"These vases came to life in a glass studio in Småland. A master glassblower shaped them freehand – straight from my sketches," recalls Maria.

IKEA PS 2026 Chair

Design Henrik Preutz

This chair has a clever twist – sit forward, lean back, spin around or rest your arms on the support. It doesn’t decide how you sit, inviting you instead to try out different options.

IKEA PS 2026 Folding chair

Design Ellen Hallström

Artistic vibes meet the warmth of birch wood. Hang it on the wall for a statement-making piece that’s more modern museum than mealtime.

IKEA PS 2026 Rack with 5 hooks

Design Ellen Hallström

This space-smart storage sidekick looks just as great whether in use or not. Its design is a modern twist on the classic Shaker peg rail, with retractable hooks that pop out when needed.

IKEA PS 2026 Table

Design Ola Wihlborg

This table is the perfect fit when you're squeezed for space. Use it as a kitchen table, craft table or even a mini-kitchen island. The hidden drawer can be opened from both sides and features a fun pop of blue inside.

IKEA PS 2026 Rug, low pile

Design Michelle Armas

Artist Michelle Armas uses a blooming ink technique to create lively, colourful designs. Inspired by her plans to visit Sweden (though she has yet to make the trip), this rug brings a Scandinavian feel to the home.

IKEA PS 2026 Floor uplighter

Design Alexander Pott

Uplighter, spotlight, floor lamp, all in one. While multifunctionality is the superpower of this lamp, three fun colour options bring a joyful addition to any space.

IKEA PS 2026 Shelving unit

Design Friso Wiersma

Inspired by the 1985 IKEA colourful classic GUIDE shelving system, this piece combines iconic design with the beauty of natural wood.

IKEA PS 2026 Footstool with storage

Design Marta Krupińska

This hand-woven rattan beauty brings a warm, earthy feel to any space. Not only is it a comfortable footstool, but it also stores items away, with easy access – out of sight, but not out of mind!

IKEA PS 2026 Table

Design Ola Wihlborg

According to Ola, round tables are a great option for small spaces. Made to mingle, this table brings everyone closer together.

IKEA PS 2026 Trolley

Design Alexander Pott

With its cake-like form in fun light blue, this trusty wheeled companion adds a touch of playfulness wherever it parks.

IKEA PS 2026 Bedside table

Design Ola Wihlborg

With its birdhouse-inspired design featuring a fold-down front and solid pine planks, this bedside table is the perfect nest for bedtime essentials.

IKEA PS 2026 Pendant lampshade

Design Lukas Bazle

Inspired by the IKEA classic GULLSUDARE, this semi-circular pendant lamp delivers both an ambient glow and a focussed downlight.

IKEA PS 2026 Wall decoration, set of 3

Design Alexander Pott

Available in two different coloured trios and made from 90% recycled paper, these friendly faces are sure to add joy to your walls.

IKEA PS 2026 Mirror

Design Ellen Hallström

With its asymmetric frame and flexible design, this metal mirror – originally imagined in wood – adds a surprising touch to any home.

IKEA PS 2026 Side table

Design David Wahl

This lightweight side table with a smart folding design opens up in a snap when you need it, then effortlessly folds away when not in use.

The story of PS

In 1995 we launched the very first IKEA PS collection, along with the concept of Democratic Design. Its five dimensions of form, function, quality and sustainability at a low price still guide how we create products today.

IKEA PS is Democratic Design in its truest form. It's our way of showing the world how much we love great design, and our dedication to making it as accessible as possible.

Although the themes of the IKEA PS collections may have varied over the years, two things remain: our Scandinavian roots and our love of simplicity. The IKEA PS 2026 collection – our tenth since 1995 – celebrates simple, useful things that bring joy to everyday living.

IKEA PS 2026 is about challenging and being playful, about creating interesting design while staying simple. It’s a collection of functional products that bend, peek, hide, snap, rock and even inflate, created to bring a smile to the home. We hope you're as excited as we are!

PS there's more!

The full IKEA PS 2026 collection is available in stores and online worldwide from 14th May. Want to get your hands on great design at an affordable price? Just click below!

Open card IKEA PS 2026 Rug, low pile Design Michelle Armas Created using a special blooming ink technique, each shape on this rug represents souls. “The flowing ink is those souls communicating," explains Michelle. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Cushion cover Design Michelle Armas This dreamy cushion cover features flowing ink shapes in vibrant shades of blue, green and orange. The Atlanta-based artist owes her love of colour to her creative upbringing in a vibrant Spanish family. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Table Design Ola Wihlborg Even a small home needs a big table sometimes! Just a quick twist of its signature red-wing screw and this folding table collapses away. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Glass-door cabinet Design Ola Wihlborg A stylish way to keep your treasures dust-free. As for the mesh – surprise! – there actually isn't any. The glass has a printed grid pattern that mimics the look of metal, minus the trouble of keeping it clean. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Vase Design Maria Vinka "These vases came to life in a glass studio in Småland. A master glassblower shaped them freehand – straight from my sketches," recalls Maria. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Chair Design Henrik Preutz This chair has a clever twist – sit forward, lean back, spin around or rest your arms on the support. It doesn’t decide how you sit, inviting you instead to try out different options. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Folding chair Design Ellen Hallström Artistic vibes meet the warmth of birch wood. Hang it on the wall for a statement-making piece that’s more modern museum than mealtime. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Rack with 5 hooks Design Ellen Hallström This space-smart storage sidekick looks just as great whether in use or not. Its design is a modern twist on the classic Shaker peg rail, with retractable hooks that pop out when needed. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Table Design Ola Wihlborg This table is the perfect fit when you're squeezed for space. Use it as a kitchen table, craft table or even a mini-kitchen island. The hidden drawer can be opened from both sides and features a fun pop of blue inside. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Rug, low pile Design Michelle Armas Artist Michelle Armas uses a blooming ink technique to create lively, colourful designs. Inspired by her plans to visit Sweden (though she has yet to make the trip), this rug brings a Scandinavian feel to the home. Open card Play video of four IKEA PS 26 uplighter lamps, moving against a pale grey background. IKEA PS 2026 Floor uplighter Design Alexander Pott Uplighter, spotlight, floor lamp, all in one. While multifunctionality is the superpower of this lamp, three fun colour options bring a joyful addition to any space. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Shelving unit Design Friso Wiersma Inspired by the 1985 IKEA colourful classic GUIDE shelving system, this piece combines iconic design with the beauty of natural wood. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Footstool with storage Design Marta Krupińska This hand-woven rattan beauty brings a warm, earthy feel to any space. Not only is it a comfortable footstool, but it also stores items away, with easy access – out of sight, but not out of mind! Open card IKEA PS 2026 Table Design Ola Wihlborg According to Ola, round tables are a great option for small spaces. Made to mingle, this table brings everyone closer together. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Trolley Design Alexander Pott With its cake-like form in fun light blue, this trusty wheeled companion adds a touch of playfulness wherever it parks. Open card Play video of a wood IKEA PS 2026 bedside table opening and closing against a pale grey background. IKEA PS 2026 Bedside table Design Ola Wihlborg With its birdhouse-inspired design featuring a fold-down front and solid pine planks, this bedside table is the perfect nest for bedtime essentials. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Pendant lampshade Design Lukas Bazle Inspired by the IKEA classic GULLSUDARE, this semi-circular pendant lamp delivers both an ambient glow and a focussed downlight. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Wall decoration, set of 3 Design Alexander Pott Available in two different coloured trios and made from 90% recycled paper, these friendly faces are sure to add joy to your walls. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Mirror Design Ellen Hallström With its asymmetric frame and flexible design, this metal mirror – originally imagined in wood – adds a surprising touch to any home. Open card IKEA PS 2026 Side table Design David Wahl This lightweight side table with a smart folding design opens up in a snap when you need it, then effortlessly folds away when not in use. The story of PS In 1995 we launched the very first IKEA PS collection, along with the concept of Democratic Design. Its five dimensions of form, function, quality and sustainability at a low price still guide how we create products today. IKEA PS is Democratic Design in its truest form. It's our way of showing the world how much we love great design, and our dedication to making it as accessible as possible. Although the themes of the IKEA PS collections may have varied over the years, two things remain: our Scandinavian roots and our love of simplicity. The IKEA PS 2026 collection – our tenth since 1995 – celebrates simple, useful things that bring joy to everyday living. IKEA PS 2026 is about challenging and being playful, about creating interesting design while staying simple. It’s a collection of functional products that bend, peek, hide, snap, rock and even inflate, created to bring a smile to the home. We hope you're as excited as we are! PS there's more! The full IKEA PS 2026 collection is available in stores and online worldwide from 14th May. Want to get your hands on great design at an affordable price? Just click below!
